articleTitle: A simplified automatic impedance matching network for electromagnetic acoustic transducers
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)

authors.preferredName: João Pedro Torres de Sousa Andrade

abstract: Electromagnetic acoustic transducers (EMATs) generate ultrasonic waves without requiring physical contact with the medium under test. Nevertheless, they present a main disadvantage of less efficiency, when compared to commonly used piezoelectric transducers, which leads to a lower signal-to-noise ratio. L-network impedance matching network is often used in order to overcome this drawback and ensure higher power transfer to the EMAT. Manually impedance matching is a laborious and time-consuming task and must be repeated whenever the transducer, specimen material, or operating frequency changes. In this paper, an automatic one-element impedance matching network was designed and its benefit in increasing the EMAT efficiency was evaluated. The theoretical optimal value for the one-element matching network was derived. Simulations confirmed its efficiency and showed that, in the analyzed scenario, it provided 90% of full, two-element, impedance matching L-network’s benefit. An automatic one-element matching network was fabricated and experimentally evaluated. The automatic system was able to determine the best configuration for the one-element matching network and provided up to 5.6 dB gain, similar to a manual solution, more than two-fold faster.

articleTitle: Design of a Low-Noise Signal Conditioning Circuit for Analog MEMS Accelerometers
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Vibration analysis in electrical machines is a widely used practice for fault identification. The most used sensor for this application is the piezoelectric accelerometer. With the advances in technology, microelectromechanical system (MEMS) accelerometers are finding use in applications traditionally dominated by piezoelectric accelerometers. However, the improvement of technology and accuracy of the sensor is useless if the signal conditioning circuit is poorly dimensioned. This paper describes the design of a low-noise signal conditioning circuit for acquiring acceleration signal provided by a MEMS accelerometer. The circuit is basically composed of a gain block implemented with an operational amplifier and a 16-bit low-noise analog-to-digital converter (ADC). After sized, the circuit was validated in an electrical simulation environment. The achieved total noise at the input of the ADC was 3.29 µV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RMS</inf> for the range of 10 kHz, which is adequate for vibration measurement application in electrical machines.

articleTitle: Instrumentation for quantum correlation analysis of polarized Stokes-anti-Stokes photon pairs
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper presents an optical spectroscopy instrumentation system engineered to measure time correlation of single photons. We explore the phenomenon of correlated Stokes-anti-Stokes (SaS) Raman scattering, analyzing the quantum nature of the phenomenon. An experimental apparatus was implemented to measure the scattering in diamond, confirming its quantum character, with the purpose of using the SaS photon pair in the codification and transmission of information.

articleTitle: Improved Self-Biased Differential Amplifiers Using Multiple-Vt CMOS Transistors
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper analyzes several self-biased topologies to implement differential amplifiers with single-ended output. Self-biased circuits potentially save area and power since they do not need dedicated current sources and mirrors. Moreover, the design is simplified because the circuit remains in the operating region independently from the transistor dimensions. These advantages come at the cost of larger sensitivity of the consumed current to process variations, this fact must be considered during design. The studied configurations are improved by using multiple-Vt (threshold voltage) transistors, which are available in conventional CMOS processes. One of the topologies is used to design an output buffer aiming to measure a rail-to-rail analog signal. The buffer is simulated in a CMOS 65nm technology and consumes 235μW with a 23MHz bandwidth in typical case. The fast and slow corner models are also accounted, resulting in worst case variations of up to 37% in power consumption. The methodology proposed shows how self-biasing can facilitate circuit design.

articleTitle: Transformer Oil Viscosity Measurements Using a Love Wave Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In this paper, a Love wave (LW) sensor is investigated as a possible device for the estimation of the quality of transformer oils. The magnitude response and the phase of the transmission coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) of the LW sensor was measured with a Vector Network Analyzer. It was shown that the viscosity of the transformer oil which is an indicator of its quality led to a reduction in the magnitude of the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> coefficient and a frequency shift. A relationship between frequency change and viscosity was identified, with higher viscosity leading to greater frequency change. Comparatively to the literature, the attenuation of the transmission coefficient is in agreement with a linear variation expected to the parameter (viscosity*density)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sup>. The study also identified the behavior of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> when observed in the time domain. The results let us conclude that LW sensors can be used as a candidate for the real time monitoring of transformers oil quality.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Decision Module for LoRa at 2.4 GHz Adaptive Network Deployment
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Long Range (LoRa) technology is a Low Power Wide Area Network (LPWAN) alternative for IoT applications. It connects devices, things, or node sensors to a gateway and then to the cloud through broadband connections. LoRa technology offers several degrees of freedom on its configuration parameters such as transmission power (PTx), spreading factor (SF), bandwidth (BW), and coding rate (CR) for different applications and use cases. According to the application, the transceiver LoRa parameters must be set up. Moreover, these parameters must be adapted or reconfigured to the current channel state, network deployment state, and optimization policies such as minimizing the node sensors’ energy consumption or maximizing the Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR). This paper proposes a fuzzy logic decision module to select the optimal configuration when conditions are changing. Rules are defined based on energy consumption and communication distance simulations using LoRa transceivers SX1280 at 2.4 GHz. We found that the decision module attributes configuration values to fit maximum communication distance while optimizing energy consumption on the node sensor.

articleTitle: MIS capacitor as portable oxygen detection sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The Oxygen (O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) gas detection is important in many activities of life and environment control. The present work proposed a photoluminescent O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor device based in the metal insulating semiconductor (MIS) capacitor. The sensor system used MIS capacitor as photodetector where it was directly integrated the active photoluminescent film. The results obtained pointed out that the proposed device exhibit high sensitivity to the presence of O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> molecules, showing non-linear response in the range of concentrations of oxygen from 0 to 100% with the most sensitive region in the range of O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentrations between 0 and 50%. This sensitivity range is within the O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration expected for applications in environmental control.

articleTitle: Tuning Key Parameters of Electric Circuit Model for Application in Solid-State Supercapacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Supercapacitors have been widely studied and used on electrical and electronic circuits as energy storage devices. The potential of using supercapacitors in engineering is being continually explored and it is essential to use models compatible with Electronic Design Automation tools. The existing models do not fully comply with the modeled device and often their use requires adjustments to bring the modeled device closer to the real one. The two branches model is one of the simplest to-use parameter calculation methods found in the literature for modeling and specifying supercapacitors of capacitances in a range of up to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> F. In this paper, it was adopted in the study of miniaturized and flexible solid-state devices with capacitances in the range of up to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> F. The result is a method applicable in specifying and simulation of tens of millifarad supercapacitors used in IoT devices using SoC technology.

articleTitle: Development of a small-scale spectrophotometer to monitor microalgae cultures on CubeSats
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the viability of utilizing Chlorella vulgaris microalgae cultures loaded onto the UERJ Sats CubeSat. The objective is to develop a compact equipment capable of real-time monitoring of (C. vulgaris) culture for potential use in a CubSat Payload. The calibration of the equipment involved using seven samples of laboratory-grown Chlorella vulgaris microalgae at different densities ranging from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> algae/mL. The calibration process included comparing the spectrophotometry readings obtained from the developed equipment with measurements obtained from a commercial benchtop spectrophotometer. Additionally, microalgae cell counting was performed using a Neubauer chamber in a Nikon optical microscope at 400x magnification. Based on the results presented in this work, it can be concluded that the spectrophotometer built at LARISA/DETEL (Laboratory of Industrial Networks and Automation Systems), utilizing the OPT101 light sensor, was successfully calibrated at LABIFI/DESMA (Laboratory of Bioremediation, Phytotechnologies and Innovation in Water and Effluent Treatment). The calibrated spectrophotometer demonstrated reliable performance on laboratory bench, showing good agreement with spectrophotometry measurements and cell counts, concerning the measurements by spectrophotometry (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = 0.9996) and with the cell count (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> = 0.988).

articleTitle: Temperature Control System for Biological Tissues in Electroporation Studies
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: It is known that biological tissues present temperature-dependent electrical conductivity. This fact has been considered in electroporation-based cancer therapies such as electrochemotherapy and ablation with irreversible electroporation, especially in pre-treatment simulations, mathematical modeling, and the development of new protocols. In this work, we proposed a novel low-cost experimental setup suitable for plate electrodes based on Peltier modules to control the temperature of the tissue sample while electroporation protocols are assessed in the laboratory. The setup was implemented and tested with liver tissue samples at two temperature setpoints. Measurements results showed the expected behavior in the electrical properties of the electroporated samples, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed setup for conducting electroporation measurements while stabilizing its temperature.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Envelope Detection for Partial Discharge Source Localization
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation of the effectiveness of envelope detection in ultra high frequency to locate partial discharge sources in high voltage equipment. Traditionally, this is carried out by the time difference of arrival method, which requires a high sampling A/D converter to acquire the instants that the signals reach the antennas. Therefore, the objective of this paper is to investigate whether envelope detection is sufficient for this purpose. Experimental tests were performed in oil cell, and four bio-inspired antennas were used to detect the phenomenon. Envelope simulations with different diode models were performed to evaluate the best model for this purpose. The results demonstrate that the envelope detection approach is promising for reducing the sample rate while maintaining acceptable accuracy in localizing PD sources.

articleTitle: Liquid Detection based on Radar Cross-Section Measurement of Love Wave Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In this article, the remote sensing of a liquid from the radar cross-section measurement of a Love wave sensor is studied. In this experiment, the Love wave sensor is monitored with a Vector Network Analyzer in a bistatic configuration. Adding a saturated NaCl solution to the sensor produces a change in the sensor impedance and in its radar cross-section of around 0.30 dBsm. A variation of the frequency of 150 kHz and the magnitude of the scattering level of 0.35 dB was measured in the operating frequency region of the sensor. The reproducibility, minimization of errors, and the time used to perform the measurement have been improved in this system.

articleTitle: A 2.4 GHz Wireless Temperature Sensor designed in 130 nm CMOS technology with 0.07 °C precision from -100 °C to 200 °C
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Temperature sensors are present in various devices, and within the context of the Internet of Things, these devices need to have low power consumption, be compact, and have an adequate linearity range for their application. Therefore, this work proposes a wireless temperature sensor developed in 130-nanometer CMOS technology, designed to operate in the ISM band at 2.4 GHz. The wireless sensor was developed using only open-source EDA tools and the Skywater 130 nm openPDK. Post-layout transient simulations were performed at different temperatures, demonstrating a precision of 0.07 C over a temperature range of -100 to 200 C, while consuming only 1.5 mW and occupying an area of 0.04 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including the RF transmitter. Furthermore, this work was compared with sensors reported in the literature. While its power consumption was similar to other sensors, its area was smaller and its maximum error was lower than most of the compared sensors. Additionally, the proposed sensor had a greater range of linearity than all of the compared sensors.

articleTitle: Design of a Multiturn RVDT with Flat-Helix Coils
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Measuring angular displacement is a common demand for many industries. In this setting, sensing technologies that minimize or eliminate measurement friction are preferable in such environments since the device’s robustness to mechanical wear reduces the need for maintenance and its costs. That includes rotary variable differential transformers (RVDTs), which stand out for their recognized good resolution and reliability. However, despite measurement quality and vast applicability, these devices present some significant drawbacks regarding their size and working range limitations. In this context, this work investigates the feasibility of a novel RVDT design. We use flat-helix coils and an amorphous alloy core as the sensor, providing a piece-wise linear angular displacement measurement without restricting rotor movement. By performing experiments with the developed prototype, it was possible to analyze, qualitatively and quantitatively, instrumentation aspects related to the proposed arrangement. Besides the capacity to perform a multiturn measurement, an average linearity coefficient of 98.75% and a mean standard deviation between experiments of approximately 1.7% were obtained, reinforcing measurement uniformity and linearity even with handmade windings and experimental setup limitations.

articleTitle: Non-Foster Circuit Compensation for Piezoelectric Energy Harvesters
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Piezoelectric energy harvesters (PEH) are transducers used for electric power generation from mechanical motion or vibration, usually modeled by power source, a resistance and a capacitance. The power transferred by the PEH can be maximized by matching its intrinsic output impedance with the load. However, because the low-frequency vibration, huge inductors are required for this purpose. Non-Fosters reactances can easily match impedances for a broad range of frequencies. This paper presents a non-Foster circuit based on a negative impedance converter for impedance matching on piezoelectric energy harvesters. The proposed circuit has been evaluated for a frequency range from 5.47 Hz to 100 Hz and the power generated has been measured on a resistive load ranging from 1 kΩ to 1 MΩ. Preliminary experimental results show an increase of 68% in power transferred to the load.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Envelope Detection for Radiometric Measurements of Partial Discharges in Instrument Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation of the effectiveness of envelope detection in detecting partial discharge signals in ultra high frequency range using a commercial circuit. Experimental tests were conducted on a defective potential transformer with a voltage class of 36 kV. The objective is to demonstrate that the approach is viable and simplifies the hardware required for signal sampling. The results show that the circuit was able to detect the signal envelope, preserving essential informations with a reduced sampling rate. This indicates that the approach is promising and can help minimize costs associated with instrumentation systems used for radiometric monitoring of partial discharges in high-voltage equipment.

articleTitle: Investigating Water Contamination with LoRa-Enabled Surface Acoustic Wave Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This article presents the development and experimental evaluation of a wireless network of Love SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) sensors for water contamination measurement in the Amazon region. The network uses a LoRa-based protocol based on RFM98 at the 433 MHz frequency band (Low Power Device). The sensor nodes rely on the mobile acoustic wave platform laboratory developed previously by our team. The instrumentation setup uses a nanoVNA to measure the S-parameters of the Love wave sensor. A Raspberry Pi collects and processes the data to obtain the essential characteristics of the sensor using a method developed in previous works. The unoptimized prototype successfully monitored a lake water quality at a node-to-node range of 700 meters for 36 hours. This work opens up opportunities for new applications in remote sensing and IoT (Internet of Things) systems for biological and health surveys in the amazonian basin.

articleTitle: A Simple Model for Dirt Deposition Classification in Insulators Based on Visible Spectrum Images
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In electrical plants, insulators suffer natural dirt deposition, which may eventually lead to electrical discharges, which can be avoided by the (costly) washing of insulators. Visual monitoring is a pragmatic approach to deciding when insulator cleaning is necessary. This study proposes a unique parameter based on the grayscale cumulative distribution for the classification of dirt deposition in four levels. This simple phenomenological model achieved similar results when compared to a more complex feature extraction approach for the same dataset of images. Furthermore, a simple affine formula was adjusted for a coarse Non-Soluble Surface Deposits estimation.

articleTitle: Detection of Small Flaws using the Potential Drop Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This work presents a non-intrusive method to detect the presence and obtain information about small flaws, caused by internal corrosion in a specimen or samples of carbon steel. The Potential Drop technique provides an electric potential gradient map, which can give information about the presence and the geometry of minor defects in the material structure. The detection of small flaws, such as cracks caused by hydrogen corrosion, was achieved using the geometry analysis of surface electric potential and current density curves. Acting similarly to an electric lens, the disturbance in the lines of current density and surface potential caused by small flaws, can provide an apparent enlargement of the dimensions of a small flaw. Observing the geometric expansion of the electrical disturbance generated by the flaw, caused by the curvature of the field lines, small flaws can be more easily detected. Diminute cracks inside a small steel specimen can be difficult to detect using traditional non-destructive testing techniques, such as ultrasound and tomography, but, the presented technique can be used as a simpler and cheaper alternative.

articleTitle: Antoniou Gyrator as a Tuner for Current Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In field applications, leakage current in high-voltage insulators is usually acquired by using current transformers (CT). Due to the multifrequency nature of the signal, gain and phase compensations are typically required for signal reconstruction but CTs have a frequency response that resembles passband filters, posing some challenges for reconstructing the original signal. To deal with that, we carried out an investigation on using a gyrator circuit as a tuner for CTs. Our goal was to determine if it could improve the frequency response and SNR of a CT with larger windings, resulting in a more well-behaved frequency range, thereby potentially facilitating the recovery of the original signal. We conclude that both a higher number of turns together with an Antoniou gyrator or a smaller number of turns are both capable of extending the frequency range for effective leakage current measuring with similar performances. While making smaller windings is cheaper, faster and easier, an equivalent performance can be achieved using the gyrator when disassembling the sensor or replacing its winding is not a viable option.

articleTitle: Current Transformer-Based System for Measuring Leakage Current
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Insulators are crucial components in high-voltage electrical systems, and their failure can result in substantial economic losses exceeding acquisition and installation costs. Failures can also overload transmission lines and cause power outages in large areas. Pollution, particularly in coastal regions, is a leading cause of insulator failure. Soluble salts like NaCl and Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> adhere to the insulator surface, creating an alternative conductive path for current leakage. In this work, a current transformer was used to develop a measurement system. The system underwent core characterization experiments and signal post-processing. The constructed prototype successfully measured and recovered the signal, demonstrating its suitability and viability for measuring leakage current in insulators. The system is capable of measuring currents ranging from hundreds of microamperes to tens of milliamperes within the frequency range of 60 Hz to 540 Hz. It enables continuous monitoring and analysis of the current in insulators.

articleTitle: Supercapacitor Portable System for Automatic Acquire of Electrical Signals, Characterization and Electrical Schematic Modeling for Microelectronic Device Application
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In this paper, new functionalities are presented for the Portable System for Automatic Acquire of Electrical Signals for Supercapacitor Characterization (SAAES<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</sup>) [1]. These supercapacitors can be used in low consumption electro-electronic devices, energy harvesting and Internet of Things (IoT) applications [2] [3] [4]. In addition to self-discharge test of supercapacitors, functions for testing galvanostatic charge and discharge cycling, automatic extraction of electrical parameters, supercapacitors circuit models and definition of test methodology were implemented. To validate the SAAES<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</sup>, it is used two supercapacitors to obtain measurements with both SAAES<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</sup> and VMP3 Multichannel Potentiostat from BioLogic [5]. Those measurements were compared, showing a mean percentage error of 0,23%.

articleTitle: Alignment precision enhancement of side-shifted dual periodic permanent magnets array with an enclosed-case electromagnetic acoustic transducer
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Shear horizontal ultrasonic guided waves are widely used in non-destructive testing and can be generated, without requiring contact with the medium under test, through periodic permanent magnets electromagnetic acoustic transducers (PPM EMATs). PPM EMATs generate both forward and backward propagating waves, which may be undesirable. Recently, we presented a non-conventional PPM-like EMAT transducer that generated waves mainly in one direction, the so-called side-shifted dual-PPM EMAT. The construction of this device, however, should be conducted with fine precision in order to avoid misalignment of its main pairs, which can hinder its unidirectional capability. In this paper, we present a robust misalignment-free enclosed-case side-shifted dual-PPM EMAT. The performance of the device was experimentally evaluated by its radiation pattern and showed similar performance to the hand-aligned device, when carefully mounted, without the need for fine manual alignment. In addition, the capacity of unidirectional generation of SH waves in plates was further experimentally illustrated. The designed unidirectional SH wave transducer can be readily used without any fine manual adjustment.

articleTitle: A Thermoelectric Generator Model validated by Different Thermal Patterns
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: The focused study on Energy Harvesting, which refers to the use of ambient energy and its conversion into electrical energy, has been intensified in order to provide a greater energy autonomy for electronic devices. Among the most varied forms of energy available in the environment, thermal energy has stood out as a source in the conversion into electrical energy, particularly by using Thermoelectric Generators (TEGs). A TEG’s generation potential in different thermal energy harvesting scenarios can be determined from a thermal emulation platform (actual scenario) or through TEG models based on electrical circuits. This work presents a comparison between the generated voltage of the TEG obtained by a proposed TEG Model and by the thermal emulation platform when the TEG is submitted to different thermal patterns. From the Mean Absolute Percentage Error metric, it was noticed — for any thermal pattern — a good and precise predictability. In fact, it demonstrated a desirable agreement between the TEG Model and the behavior observed in the thermal emulation platform.

articleTitle: Smart Water Management: a Self-Sufficient IoT-Based Application for Pressure and Flow Monitoring in Water Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Water distribution in municipalities involves various challenges, such as maintenance of pipelines, pressure and flow control, water quality monitoring, among others. In this sense, measuring the flow and pressure of a system is a key issue for optimizing water distribution in cities. Therefore, this information is important to ensure that water is delivered with quality and in adequate quantity to consumers. With the advent of technology, some advanced solutions have been proposed in the literature to address these challenges, such as hydraulic modeling software, intelligent sensors, and automated control systems. Among these, one of the most commonly used techniques to increase system efficiency is wireless sensor networks. However, monitoring in a wide coverage area, such as metropolises, becomes difficult to implement, involving high costs and infeasibility of large-scale sensor installation. Therefore, applications involving IoT (Internet of Things) have been proposed as a low-cost and low energy consumption alternative. Thus, this article describes the steps, challenges, and solutions necessary for the development of a self-sufficient IoT application aimed at monitoring pressure and flow in a water supply network.

articleTitle: Study and Development of a Battery Monitoring System (BMS) for a Formula Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In recent decades, the world has witnessed a significant increase in population growth rates, bringing the number of people living on the planet to over 8 billion. This growing number of people, along with the development of large urban centers, has resulted in a gigantic vehicle fleet, most of them powered by internal combustion engines, which operate by burning fossil fuels and generate polluting greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and methane (CH − 4). In this scenario, the generalized demand for more sustainable transportation alternatives has led vehicle manufacturers to seek to reduce the emission of pollutants by producing electric and hybrid vehicles. In this type of vehicle, the propulsion system is based on electric motors and batteries. A battery management system (BMS) is required to increase vehicle safety further. The BMS can measure parameters such as voltage, current, and temperature of the battery cells and calculate important information such as the State of Charge (SoC), State of Health (SoH), among others. Thus, this work sought to develop the hardware and software of a BMS, using as reference the BQ76PL455A-Q1 integrated circuit produced by Texas Instruments, implemented for monitoring the cells used in an accumulator of a standard competition electric vehicle SAE formula.

articleTitle: Bearing heating open-loop control system to reduce variability in BLDC motor tests
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental study on the impact of the temperature of motor bearings on test results, in a dynamometer test rig for special motor performance testing. To evaluate the relationship between the variables, an automatic test rig capable of measuring small variations of electric power was developed, adapted with a heating system for the motor bearings. The tests were performed with low-power BLDC motors (electric power of about 10 W) and with grease lubricated metal ball bearings. The results show that raising the operating temperature of the bearings to a point above that they would naturally reach during operation guarantees a fixed condition for the tests, thus reducing the variability of electric power between tests from 0.82% to 0.04%. As a consequence, the use of the temperature control system for the bearings is capable of reducing the power variability within a test, as well as guaranteeing that tests performed in different time instants are under the same condition. Those characteristics enable the possibility of performing consecutive tests and improve the reproducibility of the test results.

articleTitle: A Relative Humidity Measurement System Tolerant to Condensation Events Applied to Apple Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Measurement of relative humidity of air is crucial in refrigerated storage of fruits. Apples, for example, are stored under 90 to 95%rh air humidity and 0 to 4°C temperature. Under these conditions, it is common for the humidity sensor to face condensation episodes (dew formation), which interferes with monitoring and control. This work proposes a straightforward measurement system that tolerates high humidity rates, condensation events, and low ventilation. The system encapsulates the measurement devices in a closed structure that is automatically controlled to detect saturation and act accordingly. The results show that the proposal increases the response speed of the sensor under low ventilation conditions and improves the accuracy in detecting humidity variations when compared to other solutions in the literature.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Differential Pair Oscillator with SAW Sensor in Feedback Loop
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In this paper is presented the performance analysis of a differential pair sinusoidal oscillator with a surface acoustic wave sensor in the feedback loop. The oscillator components were selected for an oscillation frequency of 117.6 MHz and the SAW sensor model used was based on a piezoelectric crystal. The oscillator performance was verified through computer simulations by analysing the oscillation frequency and the amplitude of the the output voltage. The first analysis showed an amplitude greater than zero and an oscillation frequency close to the resonance frequency of the sensor model. Subsequently, the oscillator performance was analyzed by varying the value of one component at a time using Monte Carlo method. Based on this analysis, it was possible to determine a range of values for each component in which the output maintains oscillation. Finally, the oscillator's performance was analyzed with simultaneous variation in the values of its components. For this simulation, the range of values found in the previous analysis was used, and the variation was carried out using the Monte Carlo method. In this case, the circuit maintains oscillation in 76.8% of the iterations. These results confirm that the oscillator performance is adequate, maintaining oscillation even with variations in the values of its components.

articleTitle: IoT Sensor Node to Evaluate Indoor Air Quality in Air Conditioner Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: Indoor air quality is a critical aspect of human health, and the measurement of various parameters such as carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), carbon monoxide (CO), particulate matter with a diameter of 10 micrometers or less (PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>), particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometers or less (PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf>), and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), serves as indicators for assessing indoor air quality. This study focuses on the development of a wireless sensor node using Internet of Things (IoT) technologies and components, including the ESP32 microcontroller and Bosch BME 680 gas sensor. A comprehensive case study was conducted to investigate the impact of three key factors on indoor air quality: sensor installation height, the presence of air vents, and work shifts. The primary objective was to determine the feasibility of installing air quality meters in commercial air conditioner equipment and assess whether this approach yields comparable measurements to those obtained at the height of people’s workstations. Each factor was evaluated at two levels, and a complete factorial experiment with repetitions was performed to examine interactions among the factors. The results revealed that both sensor installation height and work shifts had a significant influence on indoor air quality and an intriguing interaction effect between work shifts and installation height was observed. Specifically, higher sensor installation heights were associated with lower pollutant concentrations. Moreover, the study found that indoor air quality tended to be poorer during the second work shift compared to the first shift. These findings provide valuable insights for the development of effective strategies for managing indoor air quality.

articleTitle: MOS Capacitor Modeling and Optimization for Fully Integrated DC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 7th International Symposium on Instrumentation Systems, Circuits and Transducers (INSCIT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a model for the rapid characterization of MOS-type capacitors in the accumulation region. Closed-form analytical expressions have been used to estimate the equivalent circuit elements, which are calculated as a function of the design parameters of the layout and of the technological process. To verify the modeling carried out, a set of MOS capacitors with different geometries were simulated in ADS® and the main characteristics of the capacitor were compared. Based on the model, an analysis/optimization was implemented in MATLAB® in order to determine the capacitor/cell layout parameters that optimize its structure, based on a figure of merit. Compared to another work in the literature, the proposed method showed a chip-area reduction of 20.82% and an ESR of 16.38% smaller for the same capacitance value. Capacitor optimization not only contributes to reducing costs but also to improving the performance of the circuit it will make part of.
